title: Variables & Basic Arithmetic #3: Algorithmic Challenge

Implement an efficient Python solution satisfying all time and memory bounds.

    data = sys.stdin.read().split()
    if not data: return
    x, y = int(data[0]), int(data[1])
    # Output (x * 3 + y) % 1000000007
    pass

if __name__ == '__main__':
    solve()

Challenge #71 in Samagra 1000 (Loops & Iterations, Stage 1):

Given two integers X and Y, compute (X * 11 + Y) modulo 10^9 + 7.
Implement an efficient Python solution satisfying all time and memory bounds.
input_format: A single line containing two space-separated integers X and Y.
output_format: Print the resulting answer to standard output.
constraints:
1 <= X, Y <= 10^6
Time Limit: 2.0s
Memory Limit: 128 MB
starter_code:
import sys

def solve():
    data = sys.stdin.read().split()
    if not data: return
    x, y = int(data[0]), int(data[1])
    # Output (x * 11 + y) % 1000000007
    pass

if __name__ == '__main__':
    solve()

Challenge #174 in Samagra 1000 (Dictionaries & Frequency, Stage 2):

Given two integers X and Y, compute (X * 24 + Y) modulo 10^9 + 7.
Implement an efficient Python solution satisfying all time and memory bounds.
input_format: A single line containing two space-separated integers X and Y.
output_format: Print the resulting answer to standard output.
constraints:
1 <= X, Y <= 10^6
Time Limit: 2.0s
Memory Limit: 128 MB
starter_code:
import sys

def solve():
    data = sys.stdin.read().split()
    if not data: return
    x, y = int(data[0]), int(data[1])
    # Output (x * 24 + y) % 1000000007
    pass

if __name__ == '__main__':
    solve()

Challenge #277 in Samagra 1000 (Basic Recursion & Edge Cases, Stage 3):

Given two integers X and Y, compute (X * 7 + Y) modulo 10^9 + 7.
Implement an efficient Python solution satisfying all time and memory bounds.
input_format: A single line containing two space-separated integers X and Y.
output_format: Print the resulting answer to standard output.
constraints:
1 <= X, Y <= 10^6
Time Limit: 2.0s
Memory Limit: 128 MB
starter_code:
import sys

def solve():
    data = sys.stdin.read().split()
    if not data: return
    x, y = int(data[0]), int(data[1])
    # Output (x * 7 + y) % 1000000007
    pass

if __name__ == '__main__':
    solve()

Challenge #448 in Samagra 1000 (Binary Search & Bounds, Stage 5):

Given two integers X and Y, compute (X * 28 + Y) modulo 10^9 + 7.
Implement an efficient Python solution satisfying all time and memory bounds.
input_format: A single line containing two space-separated integers X and Y.
output_format: Print the resulting answer to standard output.
constraints:
1 <= X, Y <= 10^6
Time Limit: 2.0s
Memory Limit: 128 MB
starter_code:
import sys

def solve():
    data = sys.stdin.read().split()
    if not data: return
    x, y = int(data[0]), int(data[1])
    # Output (x * 28 + y) % 1000000007
    pass

if __name__ == '__main__':
    solve()
